translation: Just as copper and iron, meeting dampness, produce rust that cannot be removed except by scraping and grinding, so too accumulation cannot be dispersed except by rubbing; it is the same principle. In human life, in childhood there is no accumulation; when accumulation arises, then life is cut off. In youth qi and blood are vigorous, and accumulation cannot arise. In the prime of life qi and blood are even more vigorous, but desires open up, and accumulation is hard to avoid, growing and dispersing along the way.
